Key points

An amber warning for wind covers the whole coast from 6pm tonight until 9am tomorrow.

All ferry sailings to the islands are cancelled for the rest of the day.

Gusts of up to 120 kilometres an hour are expected on exposed headlands.

14:05 Schools to close early

The county education office says all secondary schools on the coast will close at 1pm tomorrow so that pupils can get home before the strongest winds return in the afternoon. Primary schools will make their own decisions and contact parents directly by this evening.

13:20 Power company puts extra crews on standby

The regional power network says it has moved forty extra repair crews into coastal depots overnight. A spokesperson said customers who lose power should report it online rather than by phone, because the lines are likely to be busy, and should stay well away from any fallen cables.

12:10 What the amber warning means

An amber warning means there is an increased likelihood of impacts such as flying debris, damage to buildings and roads closed by fallen trees. Forecasters say the most dangerous period is likely to be between midnight and dawn, when the storm's centre passes closest to the coast.

People living close to the seafront are being advised to move cars away from the promenade and to tie down garden furniture, bins and trampolines before dark.

11:00 All island ferries cancelled

The ferry operator has cancelled every remaining sailing to the islands today, including the evening freight service. Passengers with tickets for today can travel on any sailing over the next seven days without paying extra, and the company will post an update on tomorrow's timetable at 7am.

09:30 Welcome to our live coverage

Good morning. Storm Isolde, the ninth named storm of the season, is moving north-east across the ocean and is expected to bring very strong winds and heavy rain to the coast from this evening. We will bring you the latest warnings, travel updates and advice throughout the day.
